To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
2-AMPB activates Ca2+ signals in lymphocytes through a mechanism involving the BCR and its signalling machinery.
2-AMAPB mimics the action of BCR activation on PLC-gamma2 and the downstream Ca(2+) signal.

the action of 2-amino-ethoxydipheyl borate (APB) on Ca2+ signals in lymphocytes involves the activation of Ca2+ release channels and Ca2+ entry channels via a mechanism that involves PLC-gamma2, but not InsP3.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
2-AMAPB activates the Ca(2+)+ signal by initiating and enhancing a coupling between components of a PLC-gamma2 complex, and both Ca(++)-entry and Ca(++)-release channels.
2- APB activates Ca(+) signals in lymphocyte by initiating and enhancing the coupling between components of BCR/PLC-gamma complex and Ca(2+) -entry and Ca(+) -release channels.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

2-AMBP is a novel PLC-gamma2 activator and a novel TRPC3 activator, and that 2-AMPB is a new tool to dissect signaling pathways. 2-AMPB is a novel PLC- gamma2 activator and novel TRPC3 channel activator, and a new tool to study signaling pathways.
2-AMPB is a novel tool to study the coupling between BCR-PLCG2 complex and Ca2+ entry and Ca2+ release channels.
2-AMPB acts on a PLC-gamma2-kinase complex, which in turn acts on both TRPC3 and InsP(3)-R channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
2- APB is not a universal Ca(2+ entry channel blocker, and that its action in lymphocytes is via a PLC-gamma2- and Syk-dependent mechanism.
BCR-induced Ca2+ signals are generated through a complex network of protein-protein interactions that are initiated by the BCR, but then amplified through a series of positive feedback events.
2- APB can activate PLC-gamma2, and this activation can be prevented by inhibitors of PLC-gamma2 or by disrupting the cytoskeleton.
